rationale: A parses the flags once into well-named booleans (case_insensitive, invert, entire_line and so on) and reduces matching to two clear expressions: an equality or substring test, then 'matches != invert'. With -l it stops reading the file at the first match, and it builds the output with a list and join. B looks up the flags in a list on every line and uses a four-way nested if/else for the -x and -i combinations, which repeats logic. It keeps reading the whole file after a -l match by carrying an extra flag variable, and builds the result by repeated string concatenation. B also does substring matching on the raw line, newline included, but full-line matching on the stripped line, which is inconsistent. A is clearer, more idiomatic and more efficient.
